title: Roll-forward/Haltable Canary for Optimize Recommendation Enactment
creator: Dana Park
description:
Background: The Optimize pipeline generates batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations to lower per-token cost. We need a safe enactment mechanism that can apply these recommendations automatically while giving operators an immediate halt/rollback control and ensuring detectable regressions trigger an automated pause. This ticket implements a 'roll-forward/haltable' canary that applies changes to a small traffic slice, monitors key health metrics and cost, and expands or halts based on thresholds.

Goals and scope: Implement a controllable canary controller and operator UI hooks that allow:
- staged application: traffic slices (1%, 5%, 20%) with time windows
- programmable success criteria: latency P95, error rate, quality regression signal (eval set pass rate), unit cost delta
- automatic pause and rollback on threshold breaches with human-in-the-loop resumption
- audit logging for every automated apply/rollback and operator action
- safe defaults and opt-out per-customer

Architecture notes: Introduce a Canary Controller in the rollout service that coordinates:
- dry-run simulation (cost estimate) and validation against historical traces
- traffic steering via routing policies (route tag for canary) and warmup cache priming
- telemetry gates: compare canary vs baseline on rolling windows using standard metrics surfaced in Console

Acceptance criteria:
1) Canary Controller can orchestrate a 3-stage rollout for an Optimize recommendation
2) Console shows real-time canary health and exposes a single 'Halt' button that triggers immediate rollback
3) Automated gate failures produce a reproducible rollback event and create an incident note with root-cause hints
4) Audit entries are emitted to customer logs and internal event store
5) End-to-end test coverage for canary gating logic and rollback path

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: API and controller skeleton, unit tests
- Week 2: Integration with routing and telemetry, demo with internal model
- Week 3: Console UI and audit logging, safety e2e tests
- Week 4: Canary pilot on non-critical customers, iterate

Monitoring thresholds (initial):
- Latency P95 increase > 15% -> fail
- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute -> fail
- Quality eval pass rate drop > 2% absolute -> fail
- Unit cost delta not improving by > 1% over baseline -> mark as no-op (do not progress)

Operator controls:
- Halt (immediate rollback)
- Pause (stop progress but keep canary traffic running for diagnostic window)
- Force-advance (requires 2-operator signoff)

Notes on rollback semantics: Rollback must be idempotent and must ensure KV cache consistency (evict primed keys or re-prime baseline cache). We will default to a conservative eviction strategy to avoid quality regressions.

Stakeholders: PM: Elise Tran; Design: Mateo Silva; SRE: Jordan Li; Legal/compliance: TBA

Open questions:
- Should we include simulated traffic replay as part of pre-canary validation? (prefer yes for high-risk customers)
- How to surface quality regression signals for customers using private eval pipelines?
- Multi-tenant constraints for Dedicated pools when applying per-customer recommendations
